data.name: Mabruk
data.gender_notes: Mabruk is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who has received good news or blessings. The name Mabruk carries the meaning “Blessed, Fortunate” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Mabruk usually hope their child will grow to embody blessed, fortunate and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Receiving divine blessings and good news from Allah
data.etymology: Mabruk belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Blessed, Fortunate.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mabruk total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_arabic.name: مبروك
in_arabic.long_meaning: يسعد الرب مبروك، مبروك الحمد لله على هذا الطلب، والغرض هو تقديم العبادة، والسماح بالراحة، وزيادة السعادة، ويُستخدم في مناسبات الزفاف، والولادة، والموافقة

in_urdu.name: مبروک
in_urdu.long_meaning: مبارک حمد اللہ اس کے لیے، یہ مناسبتوں پر استعمال ہوتا ہے جیسے شادی، ولادت، اور موافقت، اس کا معنی ہے خوشی اور سعادت

in_hindi.name: मबरुक
in_hindi.long_meaning: मबरुक का अर्थ है खुशी और सुख, यह नाम शादी, जन्म, और सहमति जैसी खुशी की प्रतीक गतिविधियों पर उपयोग किया जाता है, यह हिंदी में एक सुंदर और पवित्र नाम है

in_pashto.name: مبارک
in_pashto.long_meaning: مبارک پښتو دېرشمنو کې د خوشی او سعدیت په معنا سره په شادیو، پيدا کېدو او ځانګړي دغاړیو په پرتو کې کارول کېږي، دا پښتو کې د سني اسلامي کلتور سره نږدې اړیکه لري

in_english.name: Mabruk
in_english.meaning: Congratulations and good wishes, blessed event
in_english.long_meaning: Mabruk is an Arabic name that means blessed event or congratulations, it is used in various Islamic cultures to express joy and happiness during weddings, births, and other celebratory occasions, it is also associated with the Arabic root word 'baraka' meaning blessings and good tidings

pronunciation.urdu: مبارک کے اردو میں تلفظ کی تفصیل
pronunciation.hindi: मबरुक का हिन्दी में उच्चारण विवरण
pronunciation.pashto: مبارک په پښتو کې د تلفظ تفصیل

data.cultural_impact: The Arabic term "Mabruk" is a common expression of congratulations and good wishes in the Islamic culture, used to acknowledge the reception of good news or blessings in various aspects of life, such as the birth of a child, getting married, finding a job, or passing an exam. It reflects a sense of joy and unity in sharing happiness and achievements within community.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Mabruk" holds a profound spiritual significance in the Islamic faith as it emphasizes the concept of gratitude and acknowledgement of God's blessings in everyday life. By wishing someone "Mabruk," we recognize that our accomplishments and blessings originate from Allah, and remind ourselves to remain humble and thankful for His divine guidance and blessings.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Blessed, Fortunate" symbolizes One who has received good news or blessings. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Mabruk serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of blessed, fortunate.

islamic_reference.note: Traditional Islamic name with deep spiritual significance in Islamic culture

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Mabruk was the title given to the caliph Harun al-Rashid upon his successful military campaigns. The name Mabruk carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Mabruk was a title given to Harun al-Rashid in the Abbasid Caliphate.

trends: Gaining popularity in Western Muslim communities
modern_usage.modern_context: The name Mabruk remains relevant in modern Muslim society, representing a bridge between traditional Islamic values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Islamic names.

name_in_real_life.story: Fatima Mabruk, a teacher in Karachi, Pakistan, shares that their name Mabruk meaning "Blessed, Fortunate" has been a source of inspiration throughout their life, motivating them to be a positive influence in their community.
